title: Learning to Correct Geometry in Generated Videos
title_zh: 学习校正生成视频中的几何结构

paragraphs.en: Generated videos often lose geometric consistency under camera motion: structures warp under viewpoint change, parallax becomes inconsistent, and smooth camera movement may collapse into shot-like transitions. We argue that this failure is largely a data problem. In web-scale video corpora, most visible motion comes from dynamic objects captured by static or weakly moving cameras, leaving only sparse supervision for viewpoint-induced appearance changes. To address this, we propose Video Geometry Corrector ( VGC ), a post-hoc video-to-video model trained on synthetic paired supervision. Starting from real videos with diverse camera motion and pose annotations, we construct VG-Pairs with a synthetic paired-supervision data generation pipeline. Each video clip is treated as a geometry-consistent target and paired with a distorted counterpart synthesized by a pretrained image-to-video inpainting model using trajectory-adaptive keyframes. VGC learns to map the distorted input to the geometry-consistent target without modifying the source generator, and uses optical flow as an auxiliary cue to help disentangle camera motion from object motion. Experiments on pose-conditioned and prompt-driven benchmarks show that VGC improves geometric consistency across multiple source generators, and scaling to a larger backbone further extends the framework toward more general video refinement.

paragraphs.en: Recent video generation models can synthesize visually compelling clips from text, images, or video conditions Brooks et al. (2024) ; Yang et al. (2025) ; Team (2025) ; Wan et al. (2025) ; Seedance et al. (2026) ; Wu et al. (2024) ; Zhou et al. (2024) ; Zhang et al. (2026) . However, their apparent ability to behave as world simulators often breaks down once the camera moves. Rigid structures may warp under viewpoint changes, parallax may become inconsistent, scene layout may drift across frames, and continuous camera motion may collapse into shot-like transitions. These failures are especially severe under large viewpoint changes, showing that current models often generate plausible frame sequences but fail to maintain a stable 3D scene layout. We argue that camera-motion-induced geometric distortion is largely a data problem. In web-scale video corpora, most visible motion comes from dynamic objects captured by static or weakly moving cameras, leaving only sparse supervision for viewpoint-induced appearance changes. As a result, camera motion and object motion are easily entangled: when asked to generate a moving-camera shot, a model may explain the visual change by deforming scene structure rather than maintaining a stable 3D layout.

paragraphs.en: To address this problem, existing works have largely followed two directions. The first makes the generator more geometry-aware by introducing 3D supervision or spatial priors during training Bai et al. (2025) ; Wu et al. (2026) ; Kupyn et al. (2025) ; Zhang et al. (2025a) ; Ren et al. (2025) . However, as foundation models evolve rapidly and are often accessible only through checkpoints or inference APIs, modifying the source model is not always feasible. The second direction applies post-hoc video refinement Zhou et al. (2024) ; Wang et al. (2025c) ; He et al. (2024) . These methods primarily target pixel-level restoration, such as super-resolution, denoising, and temporal smoothing, thereby improving appearance without explicitly correcting the underlying geometric distortion. Post-hoc geometry correction, which requires reasoning about 3D structure under camera motion, remains comparatively underexplored.

paragraphs.en: The key bottleneck is the training data. Training a geometry corrector requires paired supervision: a geometry-distorted video and a geometry-consistent target that follows the same camera trajectory. Such pairs are nearly impossible to collect in the real world. To address this challenge, we construct the VG-Pairs dataset using a paired-supervision data generation pipeline. Starting from real videos with diverse camera motion and annotated poses, we synthesize distorted counterparts using Wan 2.1-Fun-InP, a pretrained image-to-video inpainting model based on Wan Wan et al. (2025) . Instead of conditioning only on the first and last frames, we adopt a trajectory-adaptive keyframe strategy that inserts additional keyframes at abrupt pose changes, enabling stable generation of shorter subsegments that are later stitched together. This process produces paired videos with identical semantics and similar camera motion, but different geometric fidelity.

paragraphs.en: Built on VG-Pairs , we propose Video Geometry Corrector ( VGC ), a video-to-video diffusion model that transforms geometry-distorted videos into structurally coherent outputs. VGC restores stable scene geometry without regenerating videos from scratch, preserving scene content and object appearance. To further disentangle camera motion from object motion, we incorporate optical flow as an auxiliary structural cue. Optical flow separates globally coherent camera-induced motion from local object dynamics, helping the model determine what to correct and what to preserve.

paragraphs.en: Geometry-consistent video generation. Recent video diffusion models such as Sora Brooks et al. (2024) , CogVideoX Yang et al. (2025) , HunyuanVideo Team (2025) , and Wan Wan et al. (2025) achieve strong visual quality, yet maintaining geometric consistency under camera motion remains challenging. Most existing approaches address this issue at the generator or training level. Some methods introduce explicit geometric supervision during training. GeoVideo Bai et al. (2025) incorporates depth prediction and cross-frame consistency losses. Geometry Forcing Wu et al. (2026) aligns intermediate features with pretrained 3D foundation models Wang et al. (2025d) , and Epipolar Geometry Improves Video Generation Models Kupyn et al. (2025) introduces epipolar constraints during fine-tuning. Other approaches improve geometry through post-training alignment or reward optimization. VideoGPA Du et al. (2026) derives preference signals from reprojection consistency, VideoREPA Zhang et al. (2025b) transfers physical reasoning from video foundation models, and VGGRPO An et al. (2026) extends geometry-aware rewards into latent space for dynamic scenes. A third direction incorporates explicit 3D structure into the generation pipeline. (2025c) , and SeedVR2 Wang et al. (2025b) focus on restoration and super-resolution, progressing from multi-step diffusion upscaling to single-step arbitrary-resolution enhancement. paragraphs.en: Our goal is to restore geometric consistency in generated videos under camera motion. We attribute these failures to insufficient supervision for viewpoint-induced appearance change in existing video data. Instead of modifying each video generation model to learn stronger geometric priors, we formulate geometry correction as a post-hoc video-to-video task and train a separate corrector with paired supervision. This decouples geometry correction from video generator design, making our method applicable across different model families.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的目标是在相机运动下恢复生成视频的几何一致性。 我们将这些失败归因于现有视频数据中对视角引起的外观变化监督不足。 我们没有修改每个视频生成模型以学习更强的几何先验，而是将几何校正构建为一个事后（post-hoc）的视频到视频任务，并使用成对监督训练一个单独的校正器。 这将几何校正与视频生成器设计解耦，使我们的方法可适用于不同的模型家族。

paragraphs.en: Our framework consists of two stages. First, we build VG-Pairs by synthesizing paired distorted inputs and geometry-consistent targets from real videos with diverse camera motion and pose annotations. Second, we train a video-to-video diffusion model, VGC , on these pairs to correct geometry. Optical flow extracted from the distorted input serves as an auxiliary cue for disentangling camera motion from scene dynamics.

paragraphs.en: Geometry distortions under camera motion arise in part because current video training data contains rich human and object motion, but relatively sparse supervision for viewpoint-induced appearance change. As a result, video models can confuse camera motion with scene dynamics, and may explain viewpoint change by deforming scene structure instead of preserving a stable 3D layout. Geometry correction is therefore not only a restoration problem, but also a motion disentanglement problem.
paragraphs.zh: 相机运动下的几何畸变，部分原因在于当前的视频训练数据包含丰富的人物和物体运动，但对视角引起的外观变化监督相对稀疏。 因此，视频模型可能将相机运动与场景动态混淆，并通过使场景结构变形而非保持稳定的三维布局来解释视角变化。 因此，几何校正不仅是一个修复问题，也是一个运动解耦问题。

paragraphs.en: Optical flow provides a natural auxiliary representation for this purpose. Unlike RGB frames, which entangle appearance and motion, optical flow explicitly represents motion through its location, direction, and magnitude. Camera motion tends to induce a globally coherent motion field, whereas object motion appears as local deviations from that field. We therefore compute forward optical flow between consecutive frames of the distorted input video and use it as an additional conditioning signal for the correction model. Because the flow is computed from the distorted input rather than the target, the same signal is available during both training and inference. Optical flow does not supervise the model directly; instead, it provides motion structure that helps distinguish what should be corrected from what should be preserved.

paragraphs.en: Implementation details. We construct VG-Pairs from two publicly available datasets, DL3DV Ling et al. (2024) and SpatialVID Wang et al. (2025a) . We select 9K videos from DL3DV, reserve the first 1K for evaluation, and filter 63K videos from SpatialVID that contain large camera motion. To construct paired supervision, we use Wan 2.1-Fun-InP to synthesize geometry-distorted videos from trajectory-adaptive keyframes. Given a start frame and an end frame, Wan 2.1-Fun-InP generates the intermediate video connecting them. For clips with complex camera motion, we apply this model independently to multiple keyframe-bounded subsegments and stitch the generated segments together to form the distorted training input. Because Wan’s VAE temporally compresses the video, keyframes are selected so that each generated subsegment has a frame count compatible with the temporal compression schedule. We use Wan 2.1-1.3B Wan et al. (2025) as the backbone of VGC . The model is trained for 10K steps on 32 H100 GPUs with AdamW, using a learning rate of 1 × 10 − 5 1\times 10^{-5} , weight decay 0.01 0.01 , and a global batch size of 64. paragraphs.en: Evaluation datasets and metrics. To evaluate VGC ’s performance, we study two scenarios in which camera motion is introduced. In the first setting, camera motion is specified by camera poses. Following Geometry Forcing Wu et al. (2026) , we evaluate on RealEstate10K Zhou et al. (2018) using 100 randomly sampled test videos and DFoT Song et al. (2025) as the source generator. We compare against Geometry Forcing and Geometry Forcing + REPA Yu et al. (2025) , and report PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS Zhang et al. (2018) , and revisit error (RVE). Following Wu et al. (2026) , RVE measures long-range consistency under a full camera rotation by comparing the generated view at the end of the trajectory with the corresponding reference view. In the second setting, camera motion is induced by the text prompt. We use three source generators in this setting: CogVideoX-5B I2V, CogVideoX-5B T2V, and CogVideoX 1.5-5B T2V. We randomly sample 200 prompts from the held-out DL3DV test set. Following VideoGPA Du et al. (2026) , we reconstruct each generated video independently using Depth Anything 3 Lin et al. (2026) and compare its original frames with frames reprojected from the reconstructed 3D geometry to compute PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS Zhang et al. (2018) , MSE, and 3D consistency score (3DCS). Unlike the pose-conditioned setting, these metrics do not require ground-truth video frames. In both settings, VGC is applied as a post-hoc corrector to the outputs of the source generator, demonstrating its flexibility across different video model families.
paragraphs.zh: 评测数据集与指标。 为了评估 VGC 的性能，我们研究了两种引入相机运动的场景。 在第一种设置中，相机运动由相机位姿指定。 按照 Geometry Forcing（Wu 等人， 2026）的做法，我们在 RealEstate10K（Zhou 等人， 2018）上使用 100 个随机采样的测试视频进行评测，并以 DFoT（Song 等人， 2025）作为源生成器。 我们与 Geometry Forcing 以及 Geometry Forcing + REPA（Yu 等人， 2025）进行比较，并报告 PSNR、SSIM、LPIPS（Zhang 等人， 2018）以及重访误差（RVE）。按照 Wu 等人 （2026）的做法，RVE 通过将轨迹末端生成的视图与对应的参考视图进行比较，来衡量完整相机旋转下的长程一致性。 在第二种设置中，相机运动由文本提示引发。 我们在此设置中使用三个源生成器：CogVideoX-5B I2V、CogVideoX-5B T2V 和 CogVideoX 1.5-5B T2V。 我们从留出的 DL3DV 测试集中随机采样 200 条提示。 按照 VideoGPA（Du 等人， 2026）的做法，我们使用 Depth Anything 3（Lin 等人， 2026）对每个生成的视频独立进行重建，并将原始帧与从重建的 3D 几何重投影得到的帧进行比较，以计算 PSNR、SSIM、LPIPS（Zhang 等人， 2018）、MSE 以及 3D 一致性得分（3DCS）。 与位姿条件设置不同，这些指标不需要真值视频帧。 在这两种设置中，VGC 都被作为事后校正器应用于源生成器的输出，展示了其在不同视频模型家族之间的灵活性。

paragraphs.en: We further investigate whether the proposed correction framework can extend beyond geometry correction in static scenes. To this end, we train a larger version of VGC based on Wan 2.2-14B and evaluate it in a more general video refinement setting. With increased model capacity, VGC not only corrects geometric distortions under camera motion, but also improves dynamic videos by recovering more plausible human and object geometry. As shown in Figure 6 , the smaller 1.3B version does not exhibit the same ability to recover dynamic motion. Because the 14B model takes 480p videos as input and produces 720p outputs, it also performs super-resolution as part of the refinement process.
paragraphs.zh: 我们进一步研究所提出的校正框架能否超越静态场景中的几何校正。 为此，我们基于 Wan 2.2-14B 训练了一个更大版本的 VGC，并在更通用的视频精修设置下对其进行评估。 随着模型容量的增加，VGC 不仅能在相机运动下校正几何畸变，还能通过恢复更合理的人体和物体几何来改善动态视频。 如图 6 所示，较小的 1.3B 版本并未表现出同样的动态运动恢复能力。 由于 14B 模型以 480p 视频作为输入并生成 720p 输出，它还在精修过程中执行了超分辨率。

paragraphs.en: For evaluation, we randomly sample 100 held-out videos from SpatialVID Wang et al. (2025a) and compare against general video refinement methods, including SeedVR2 Wang et al. (2025b) and VEnhancer v2 He et al. (2024) . To demonstrate the flexibility of VGC , we apply it to videos generated by three different source models: CogVideoX Yang et al. (2025) , HunyuanVideo 1.5 Team (2025) , and Wan 2.1 Wan et al. (2025) . CogVideoX and HunyuanVideo 1.5 are evaluated in the image-to-video setting, while Wan 2.1 is evaluated in the inpainting setting. Since these videos contain dynamic content and do not admit a geometry-consistent reconstruction target, we evaluate them with no-reference video-quality metrics rather than reconstruction metrics. Specifically, we report VBench Huang et al. (2024) metrics together with DOVER Wu et al. (2023) , a holistic no-reference video-quality metric that summarizes technical and aesthetic quality.

paragraphs.en: We presented Video Geometry Corrector ( VGC ), a post-hoc video-to-video model for correcting geometric distortions in generated videos under camera motion. We argued that these failures are largely a data problem: current video training data provides limited supervision for viewpoint-induced appearance change, causing camera motion to be entangled with scene dynamics. To address this, we constructed VG-Pairs from real videos with diverse camera motion and trained VGC to map geometry-distorted videos to geometry-consistent targets. We further incorporated optical flow as an auxiliary cue to help distinguish what should be corrected from what should be preserved. Experiments on pose-conditioned and prompt-driven benchmarks show that VGC improves geometric consistency across different source generators and can be flexibly combined with existing geometry-aware methods. With increased model capacity, the same correction framework also extends beyond static-scene geometry toward more general video refinement.
